newsitem.title: INDIA: SocGen-Crosby sees Indian industry reviving.
newsitem.headline: SocGen-Crosby sees Indian industry reviving.

text.p: Securities firm SocGen-Crosby Securities said it saw first signs of an industrial revival in India.
"There are now tentative signs that the industrial sector has bottomed out," it said in a South Asia Economic Review.
Although official data on industrial growth will be available only after a lag of several months, three indicators pointed to an industrial revival, the research report said.
The three indicators are non-oil imports, freight rate for trucks on major routes and credit creation by banks.
Non-oil imports are recovering, the report said.

It said non-oil imports rose 5.5 percent year on year in October 1997 after four months of negative growth. Non-oil imports are strong indicators of industrial health because the category is mostly made up of capital goods and industrial inputs. The revival in non-oil imports suggests that the industry is again beginning to suck in imports, it said.
The report said freight rates on major truck routes rose.

It said freight rates on three of India's major highway routes were rising steadily. Freight rates for trucks have a close link with the level of economic activity because the state-owned railway system is very unresponsive to sudden changes in demand/supply.

The rates seem to have bottomed out in September/October 1996 and have been rising steadily since mid-November. For example, the rates on the Delhi-Bombay route rose 19 percent between mid-November 1996 and mid-December 1996, SocGen-Crosby said.
Informal discussions with truck operators suggest that they are likely to rise even further in the next few weeks.

It said credit creation was expected to gather momentum soon. Unlike the other two lead indicators, credit creation is yet to show a strong positive trend. Although absolute levels of credit have risen significantly since September 1996, this is largely due to seasonal factors unrelated to industrial revival.

"But we expect even this will rise sharply in the next few weeks. Overall, we expect an industrial revival in second half of 1996/97 (April-March) to feed into a 8.0-9.0 percent expansion in industrial production for the year as a whole," the report said.

"This will combine with robust agricultural expansion to keep GDP growth at 6.1 percent. Further, we expect an industrial expansion of 9.0-10.0 percent in FY98 will push up GDP growth to 6.5 percent," the SocGen-Crosby research report said.
